    foreground: ink
    primary: blue

  # No font is named beyond the one above, so nothing is fetched from a font

  typography:

      weight: bold

  opts_chunk:
    echo: false
    message: false

  # A chunk that fails stops the render, which is Quarto's default. Named

```{r setup}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What to set for a report
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The path to the config file, whose sts section names the Bronze layer of
# the module. A chunk runs with the directory of this template as its working
# directory, which is inside the installed package, so the path is taken from
# the environment variable FINCOMMONS_CONFIG where it is set and is otherwise
# a paths.yaml beside the template.
config_path <- Sys.getenv("FINCOMMONS_CONFIG", "paths.yaml")

# The snapshot the report is about, as the day it was collected on, or NULL
# for the most recent one the lake holds. FINCOMMONS_SNAPSHOT wins where it
# is set, so that a run reporting one snapshot after another needs no edit of
# the template.
report_snapshot <- NULL
if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("FINCOMMONS_SNAPSHOT"))) {
  report_snapshot <- Sys.getenv("FINCOMMONS_SNAPSHOT")
}

# The snapshot this one is compared with, or NULL for the one before it.
# This is the only way to see what left the register: the register itself
# answers for the day it is read and ESMA has published no record of a
# removal since May 2022.
compare_snapshot <- NULL

# How many rows a ranking shows.
top_n <- 15

# The point size of the text in a chart.
chart_base_size <- 9

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The corporate design
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# You can adapt your corporate design in the sourced R script. It is one file
# for the whole package, in the templates directory at the root of it, so
# that a report of any module looks like the others and a change to the
# design is made once. A copy beside this template wins over it, which is
# what lets a template taken out of the package carry a design of its own.
library(ggplot2)
design_file <- "r-corporate-design-functions-ggplot2.R"
design_path <- c(design_file, file.path("..", "..", "templates", design_file))
design_path <- design_path[file.exists(design_path)]
if (length(design_path) == 0) {
  stop("The corporate design script ", design_file, " is neither beside this ",
       "template nor in the templates directory of the package.")
}
source(design_path[1])

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(yaml)
library(jsonlite)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reading a snapshot
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# A field of a register document may hold one value or several, and the
# several arrive as a JSON array. Everything this report reads is read
# through these two, so that a field that becomes multi-valued does not
# silently turn a column into a list.
one_chr <- function(value) {
  if (is.null(value) || length(value) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  as.character(value[[1]])
}
all_chr <- function(value) {
  if (is.null(value) || length(value) == 0) return(character(0))
  as.character(unlist(value, use.names = FALSE))
}

# The day part of a Solr date, which arrives as 2026-09-10T00:00:00Z.
as_day <- function(value) as.Date(substr(value, 1, 10))

# The scheme a securitisation identifier belongs to. Only the first joins to
# anything outside the register: it is the identifier the disclosure
# templates use, the reporting entity's legal entity identifier, a letter for
# the class and the period. A private notification carries a synthetic
# identifier instead, and three notifications carry nothing at all.
identifier_scheme <- function(value) {
  trimmed <- trimws(ifelse(is.na(value), "", value))
  dplyr::case_when(
    trimmed == "" ~ "missing",
    grepl("^[A-Z0-9]{20}[A-Z][0-9]{6}$", trimmed) ~ "LEI and period",
    grepl("^SYSEC", trimmed, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "synthetic list",
    grepl("^PRIVATE", trimmed, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "private placeholder",
    TRUE ~ "other")
}

yaml_paths <- read_yaml(config_path)
path_bronze <- yaml_paths[["sts"]][["bronze"]]

# A layer may be given as a mapping carrying a path and a table name. R reads
# files, so it takes the path.
if (is.list(path_bronze)) path_bronze <- path_bronze[["path"]]
if (is.null(path_bronze)) {
  stop("The configuration file ", config_path, " gives no bronze layer for ",
       "the sts module.")
}

path_register <- file.path(path_bronze, "register")
snapshots_held <- sort(list.dirs(path_register, full.names = FALSE,
                                 recursive = FALSE))
snapshots_held <- snapshots_held[grepl("^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$",
                                       snapshots_held)]

if (length(snapshots_held) == 0) {
  stop("The Bronze layer of the sts module holds no snapshot of the ",
       "register. Collect one first: sts.update_bronze_sts('",
       config_path, "')")
}

if (is.null(report_snapshot)) {
  report_snapshot <- snapshots_held[length(snapshots_held)]
} else if (!report_snapshot %in% snapshots_held) {
  stop("The Bronze layer holds no snapshot of ", report_snapshot,
       ". It holds ", paste(snapshots_held, collapse = ", "), ".")
}

earlier <- snapshots_held[snapshots_held < report_snapshot]
if (is.null(compare_snapshot) && length(earlier) > 0) {
  compare_snapshot <- earlier[length(earlier)]
}

# One snapshot, read into a table of notifications and a table of children.
# The pages are read as lists rather than simplified into data frames: a page
# holds up to 258 fields of which a notification carries as few as sixteen,
# and simplification would bind pages of different shapes.
read_documents <- function(day, kind) {
  pages <- sort(list.files(file.path(path_register, day),
                           pattern = paste0("^", kind, "-.*\\.json$"),
                           full.names = TRUE))
  if (length(pages) == 0) return(list())
  documents <- list()
  for (page in pages) {
    answer <- fromJSON(page, simplifyVector = FALSE)
    documents <- c(documents, answer$response$docs)
  }
  documents
}

read_notifications <- function(day) {
  documents <- read_documents(day, "parent")
  if (length(documents) == 0) {
    stop("The snapshot of ", day, " holds no notification.")
  }
  tibble(
    id = vapply(documents, function(d) one_chr(d$id), character(1)),
    securitisation = vapply(documents,
                            function(d) one_chr(d$stsre_sec_id), character(1)),
    notification = vapply(documents,
                          function(d) one_chr(d$stsre_notif_id), character(1)),
    type = vapply(documents,
                  function(d) one_chr(d$stsre_sectype_desc), character(1)),
    class = vapply(documents,
                   function(d) one_chr(d$stsre_secclass_desc), character(1)),
    status = vapply(documents,
                    function(d) one_chr(d$stsre_compl_stat_desc),
                    character(1)),
    sanction = vapply(documents,
                      function(d) one_chr(d$stsre_sanc_status), character(1)),
    exposure = vapply(documents,
                      function(d) one_chr(d$stsre_undrlexp_desc),
                      character(1)),
    first_notified = as_day(vapply(documents,
                                   function(d) one_chr(d$stsre_init_notif_dt),
                                   character(1))),
    notified = as_day(vapply(documents,
                             function(d) one_chr(d$stsre_notif_dt),
                             character(1))),
    name = vapply(documents,
                  function(d) one_chr(d$stsre_sec_name), character(1)),
    repository = vapply(documents,
                        function(d) one_chr(d$stsre_sec_repository),
                        character(1)),
    reporting_entity = vapply(documents,
                              function(d) one_chr(d$de_name), character(1)),
    reporting_lei = vapply(documents,
                           function(d) one_chr(d$de_lei_priv), character(1)),
    verifier = vapply(documents,
                      function(d) one_chr(d$authorised_third_party_name),
                      character(1)),
    again = vapply(documents,
                   function(d) one_chr(d$multiple_notif_reason_desc),
                   character(1)),
    fields = vapply(documents, length, integer(1))
  ) %>%
    mutate(scheme = identifier_scheme(securitisation))
}

read_children <- function(day) {
  documents <- read_documents(day, "child")
  if (length(documents) == 0) return(tibble())
  bind_rows(lapply(documents, function(d) {
    kind <- one_chr(d$entity_type)
    identifier <- switch(
      kind,
      issins = one_chr(d$stsre_isin_instrument),
      originator = one_chr(d$originator_lei),
      lender = one_chr(d$lender_lei),
      sponsor = one_chr(d$sponsor_lei),
      sspe = NA_character_,
      NA_character_)
    label <- switch(
      kind,
      issins = one_chr(d$stsre_isin_name),
      originator = one_chr(d$originator_name),
      lender = one_chr(d$lender_name),
      sponsor = one_chr(d$sponsor_name),
      sspe = one_chr(d$sspe_country_name),
      NA_character_)
    country <- switch(
      kind,
      originator = one_chr(d$originator_country),
      lender = one_chr(d$lender_country),
      sponsor = one_chr(d$sponsor_country),
      sspe = one_chr(d$sspe_country_code),
      NA_character_)
    tibble(parent = one_chr(d$`_root_`), kind = kind,
           identifier = identifier, label = label, country = country)
  }))
}

# The census of the fields the notifications carry: every field name and how
# many notifications carry it. The record the collection wrote holds the same
# census; it is counted again here so that the report stands on the snapshot
# rather than on the record beside it.
field_census <- function(day) {
  documents <- read_documents(day, "parent")
  names_seen <- unlist(lapply(documents, names), use.names = FALSE)
  as_tibble(table(names_seen)) %>%
    rename(field = names_seen, notifications = n) %>%
    arrange(desc(notifications), field)
}

notifications <- read_notifications(report_snapshot)
children <- read_children(report_snapshot)
census <- field_census(report_snapshot)

# The record the collection wrote, where it is there. It carries what the
# portal said it held, which is how the report can say whether the snapshot
# is complete rather than merely how much of it there is.
record_path <- file.path(path_bronze, "collections",
                         paste0("register-", report_snapshot, ".json"))
record <- if (file.exists(record_path)) {
  fromJSON(record_path, simplifyVector = FALSE)
} else {
  NULL
}

n_notifications <- nrow(notifications)
n_public <- sum(notifications$type == "Public", na.rm = TRUE)
n_private <- sum(notifications$type == "Private", na.rm = TRUE)
n_joinable <- sum(notifications$scheme == "LEI and period", na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r title, results='asis'}
typst_document_title(paste0("STS register report, snapshot of ", report_snapshot))
```

# The register of STS securitisations

```{r opening, results='asis'}
stated <- if (!is.null(record)) {
  parents <- record$stated_totals$parent
  kids <- record$stated_totals$child
  paste0(" The portal stated ", format(parents, big.mark = ","),
         " notifications and ", format(kids, big.mark = ","),
         " child documents when it was collected, and the snapshot holds ",
         format(n_notifications, big.mark = ","), " and ",
         format(nrow(children), big.mark = ","), ".")
} else {
  ""
}

cat(paste0(
  "This report is about one snapshot of the public register ESMA keeps of ",
  "the securitisations notified to it as simple, transparent and ",
  "standardised: the snapshot of **", report_snapshot, "**, which holds **",
  format(n_notifications, big.mark = ","), " notifications** and **",
  format(nrow(children), big.mark = ","), " child documents** carrying their ",
  "tranches and their parties.", stated, "\n\n",
  "**The register is current state, and this is the thing to know before ",
  "reading any figure here.** It answers for what is STS on the day it is ",
  "read and for nothing else: a cancelled notification leaves it, and the ",
  "two spreadsheets in which ESMA recorded removals were frozen in 2022. So ",
  "a count below is a count of a register as it stood on one day, not of ",
  "everything ever notified, and the only way to see what has left is to ",
  "set two snapshots side by side, which the section on what changed does.\n"))
```

## The register at a glance

```{r glance}
glance <- tibble(
  What = c("Notifications", "Public", "Private",
           "Identifier that joins to reported data",
           "Child documents", "Distinct securitisation identifiers",
           "Fields seen across the notifications"),
  Count = c(n_notifications, n_public, n_private, n_joinable,
            nrow(children),
            length(unique(trimws(notifications$securitisation))),
            nrow(census)))

knitr::kable(glance, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
             caption = paste("The snapshot of", report_snapshot))
```

```{r populations, results='asis'}
public_fields <- notifications$fields[notifications$type == "Public"]
private_fields <- notifications$fields[notifications$type == "Private"]
# A public notification with no child document at all belongs to neither
# population: it is marked public and filled in like a private one. The same
# count appears among the checks at the end, by the same definition.
bare <- notifications %>%
  filter(type == "Public", !id %in% children$parent) %>%
  nrow()

cat(paste0(
  "**Two populations.** A public notification carries the whole STS ",
  "template, its tranches and its parties; a private one carries the core ",
  "and no child document at all. In this snapshot a public notification ",
  "carries a median of ", median(public_fields), " fields and a private one ",
  median(private_fields), ". The difference is not a matter of degree: it ",
  "decides whether a notification can be joined to anything at all.\n"))

if (bare > 0) {
  cat(paste0(
    "\n", bare, " notification", if (bare == 1) " is" else "s are",
    " marked public and carr", if (bare == 1) "ies" else "y",
    " no more than a private one does -- no template and no child ",
    "document. ", if (bare == 1) "It is" else "They are",
    " counted again among the checks at the end, being neither population ",
    "nor an error this report can resolve.\n"))
}
```

```{r class-and-type}
knitr::kable(
  notifications %>%
    count(class, type) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = n, values_fill = 0L) %>%
    mutate(Total = rowSums(across(where(is.numeric)))) %>%
    arrange(desc(Total)),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "Notifications by class and by whether the deal is public")
```

## What the securitisations are backed by

```{r exposures-data}
# The register names an exposure in the wording of the technical standards,
# which runs to ninety-eight characters for the longest of the eight. The
# label is wrapped rather than cut -- a label shortened here would be a
# category of this report's making rather than one of the register's -- and
# the chart is given the height that costs: a wrapped label needs more room
# than the space between two bars, and the bars are spaced by the height.
exposures <- notifications %>%
  mutate(exposure = ifelse(is.na(exposure), "not stated", exposure)) %>%
  count(exposure, sort = TRUE)

# What the alt text of the chart says: every exposure and its count, in the
# order of the bars, which is what a sighted reader takes from it.
alt_exposures <- paste0(
  "Horizontal bar chart of the ", format(n_notifications, big.mark = ","),
  " notifications in the snapshot of ", report_snapshot,
  " by the underlying exposure they are backed by, largest first, with the count ",
  "printed at the end of each bar: ",
  paste0(exposures$exposure, " ", format(exposures$n, big.mark = ","), collapse = "; "), ".")

exposures <- exposures %>%
  mutate(exposure = wrap_labels(exposure, 40),
         exposure = factor(exposure, levels = rev(exposure)))
```

```{r exposures}
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-alt: !expr alt_exposures
ggplot(exposures, aes(x = n, y = exposure)) +
  geom_col(fill = palette_corporate_design("cat", 1)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.2, size = chart_base_size / 3.2) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       title = "The underlying exposures of the notified securitisations",
       caption = caption_corporate_design(
         source = "ESMA STS register", last = report_snapshot, lang = "en")) +
  theme_corporate_design(base_size = chart_base_size, grid = "x")
```

## When they were notified

```{r notified-when-data}
by_year <- notifications %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(format(first_notified, "%Y"))) %>%
  count(year, type)

# What the alt text of the chart says: the count of every year, public and
# private apart, and the year each peaked in.
alt_by_year <- paste0(
  "Column chart in ", n_distinct(by_year$type), " panels, one per type of notification (",
  paste(sort(unique(by_year$type)), collapse = " and "), "), of the notifications in the ",
  "snapshot of ", report_snapshot, " by the year of their first notification, from ",
  min(by_year$year, na.rm = TRUE), " to ", max(by_year$year, na.rm = TRUE),
  ", with the count printed above each column. ",
  paste(vapply(split(by_year, by_year$type), function(d) {
    d <- d[!is.na(d$year), ]
    paste0(d$type[1], ": ", paste0(d$year, " ", d$n, collapse = ", "),
           "; the most in ", d$year[which.max(d$n)], ".")
  }, character(1)), collapse = " "))
```

```{r notified-when}
#| fig-height: 2.6
#| fig-alt: !expr alt_by_year
# Public and private are drawn side by side rather than stacked, so that the
# panel names the type and its colour does not have to; the count is printed
# above each column.
ggplot(by_year, aes(x = year, y = n, fill = type)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.4, size = chart_base_size / 3.4,
            colour = design_colours()[["ink"]]) +
  facet_wrap(~ type) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_accessible) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(by_year$year))) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "First notification, by the year it was made in",
       caption = caption_corporate_design(
         source = "ESMA STS register", last = report_snapshot, lang = "en")) +
  theme_corporate_design(base_size = chart_base_size, grid = "y")
```

```{r notified-note, results='asis'}
updated <- sum(notifications$notified != notifications$first_notified,
               na.rm = TRUE)
cat(paste0(
  "The register carries the day a securitisation was first notified and the ",
  "day its notification last moved. The two differ on **",
  format(updated, big.mark = ","), " of ",
  format(n_notifications, big.mark = ","),
  "** notifications, so a notification is not a thing said once; ",
  sum(!is.na(notifications$again)),
  " of them state a reason for having been notified again.\n"))
```

## The identifiers

```{r schemes}
knitr::kable(
  notifications %>%
    count(scheme, sort = TRUE) %>%
    rename(Scheme = scheme, Notifications = n),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = paste("The schemes the securitisation identifiers follow.",
                  "Only the first joins to data reported under the",
                  "disclosure templates."))
```

```{r identifier-uniqueness, results='asis'}
trimmed <- trimws(ifelse(is.na(notifications$securitisation), "",
                         notifications$securitisation))
repeated <- sum(table(trimmed[trimmed != ""]) > 1)
cat(paste0(
  "**Neither identifier here identifies a row.** The ",
  format(n_notifications, big.mark = ","), " notifications carry ",
  format(length(unique(trimmed)), big.mark = ","),
  " distinct securitisation identifiers and ",
  format(length(unique(trimws(notifications$notification))),
         big.mark = ","),
  " distinct notification identifiers: ", repeated,
  " securitisation identifiers appear on more than one notification, a ",
  "securitisation being notified again when it is restructured or ",
  "re-notified. The register's own document id is what identifies a row, ",
  "and any join on the securitisation identifier is one to many.\n"))
```

## The tranches and the parties

```{r parties}
kinds <- tibble(
  kind = c("issins", "originator", "sspe", "lender", "sponsor"),
  What = c("Tranches, by ISIN", "Originators", "Special purpose entities",
           "Original lenders", "Sponsors"))

knitr::kable(
  kinds %>%
    left_join(
      children %>%
        group_by(kind) %>%
        summarise(Rows = n(),
                  Notifications = n_distinct(parent),
                  Identified = sum(!is.na(identifier)),
                  Distinct = n_distinct(identifier[!is.na(identifier)]),
                  .groups = "drop"),
      by = "kind") %>%
    select(-kind) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ tidyr::replace_na(.x, 0L))),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = paste("The child documents of the snapshot. 'Identified' counts",
                  "the rows carrying an ISIN or a legal entity identifier."))
```

```{r parties-note, results='asis'}
cat(paste0(
  "The tranches carry ISINs, which join to `fincommons.firds`, and the ",
  "originator, the original lender and the sponsor carry legal entity ",
  "identifiers, which join to `fincommons.entitymasterdata`. **The special ",
  "purpose entity carries a country and nothing else** -- no identifier and ",
  "no name -- which is a gap in the register rather than in the reading of ",
  "it. Children hang off a notification by the register's document id; they ",
  "carry no identifier of their own, so a tranche is reached through its ",
  "notification.\n"))
```

```{r originators}
if (any(children$kind == "originator")) {
  knitr::kable(
    children %>%
      filter(kind == "originator", !is.na(label)) %>%
      count(label, sort = TRUE) %>%
      head(top_n) %>%
      rename(Originator = label, Notifications = n),
    caption = paste("The originators named in most notifications, of",
                    n_distinct(children$identifier[children$kind ==
                                                     "originator"]),
                    "with a legal entity identifier"))
}
```

## What the notifications say of themselves

```{r census-prepare}
# Solr's own bookkeeping -- the document key, the version, the time the index
# was written -- is on every document of every register and says nothing
# about a notification, so the census shown is of the register's own fields.
# It is counted out rather than dropped from the snapshot, which keeps what
# was published.
internal <- c("_root_", "_version_", "timestamp", "type_s", "entity_type")
register_census <- census %>% filter(!field %in% internal)
on_every <- sum(register_census$notifications == n_notifications)
```

```{r census, results='asis'}
cat(paste0(
  "A notification in this snapshot carries one of ", nrow(register_census),
  " field names, beside the ", length(internal),
  " the register keeps for its own bookkeeping. ", on_every,
  " of them are on every notification -- the identifiers, the class, the ",
  "type, the status and the dates -- and the rest are the STS template, ",
  "which only a public notification fills in. The table below is the head ",
  "of the census the collection wrote beside the snapshot: comparing it ",
  "with an older one is how a change to the register is noticed.\n"))
```

```{r census-table}
knitr::kable(
  register_census %>%
    head(top_n) %>%
    mutate(share = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * notifications / n_notifications)) %>%
    rename(Field = field, Notifications = notifications, Share = share),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "The fields most notifications carry")
```

```{r verifiers}
if (any(!is.na(notifications$verifier))) {
  knitr::kable(
    notifications %>%
      filter(!is.na(verifier)) %>%
      count(verifier, sort = TRUE) %>%
      head(top_n) %>%
      rename(`Third-party verifier` = verifier, Notifications = n),
    caption = paste("The authorised third parties that verified STS",
                    "compliance, as the notifications name them. The names",
                    "are not normalised in the register: one verifier",
                    "appears under several spellings."))
}
```

## What changed since the snapshot before

```{r changed, results='asis'}
if (is.null(compare_snapshot)) {
  cat(paste0(
    "The lake holds one snapshot of the register, so there is nothing to ",
    "compare it with yet. **This is the section that makes the Bronze layer ",
    "worth keeping.** The register publishes no history and ESMA's two ",
    "spreadsheets of removals were frozen in 2022, so from here on the only ",
    "record of a notification leaving the register is that it was in one ",
    "snapshot and not in the next. Collect again, and this section will say ",
    "what arrived and what went.\n"))
} else {
  before <- read_notifications(compare_snapshot)
  arrived <- setdiff(notifications$id, before$id)
  departed <- setdiff(before$id, notifications$id)
  cat(paste0(
    "Against the snapshot of **", compare_snapshot, "**, which held ",
    format(nrow(before), big.mark = ","), " notifications: **",
    length(arrived), " arrived** and **", length(departed), " left**.\n\n",
    "A notification that has left the register has not necessarily been ",
    "cancelled -- the register gives no reason, which is why what left is ",
    "recorded here as a fact about two snapshots and nothing more.\n"))
}
```

```{r changed-table}
if (!is.null(compare_snapshot)) {
  before <- read_notifications(compare_snapshot)
  departed <- before %>% filter(!id %in% notifications$id)
  if (nrow(departed) > 0) {
    knitr::kable(
      departed %>%
        select(securitisation, type, class, name, first_notified) %>%

               Name = name, `First notified` = first_notified),
```

## What to expect of the data

```{r quality}
blank <- sum(trimws(ifelse(is.na(notifications$securitisation), "",
                           notifications$securitisation)) == "")
untrimmed <- sum(!is.na(notifications$securitisation) &
                   notifications$securitisation !=
                   trimws(notifications$securitisation))
duplicated_ids <- notifications %>%
  mutate(key = trimws(securitisation)) %>%
  filter(key != "") %>%
  add_count(key) %>%
  filter(n > 1)
childless_public <- notifications %>%
  filter(type == "Public", !id %in% children$parent) %>%
  nrow()
isins <- children$identifier[children$kind == "issins"]
malformed_isin <- sum(!is.na(isins) &
                        !grepl("^[A-Z]{2}[A-Z0-9]{9}[0-9]$", isins))
missing_isin <- sum(is.na(isins))
constant <- census %>%
  filter(field == "stsre_sanc_status") %>%
  pull(notifications)

checks <- tibble(
  Check = c(
    "Notifications whose securitisation identifier is blank",
    "Identifiers carrying leading or trailing space",
    "Notifications sharing an identifier with another",
    "Of those, stating no reason for the second notification",
    "Public notifications with no child document at all",
    "Tranche rows carrying no ISIN",
    "ISINs that are not well formed",
    "Distinct values of the sanction status"),
  Count = c(
    blank, untrimmed, nrow(duplicated_ids),
    sum(is.na(duplicated_ids$again)), childless_public,
    missing_isin, malformed_isin,
    n_distinct(notifications$sanction)))

knitr::kable(checks, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
             caption = paste("Counted over the snapshot of", report_snapshot))
```

```{r quality-note, results='asis'}
cat(paste0(
  "None of these is a fault of the pipeline: each is what the register ",
  "says, and the Bronze layer keeps it as it was published. They are listed ",
  "because each one decides something about reading the data. A blank ",
  "identifier cannot be joined; an identifier with a leading space joins to ",
  "nothing unless it is trimmed; an identifier on two notifications makes ",
  "every join one to many; and a sanction status with one distinct value -- ",
  "`", notifications$sanction[1], "` on all ",
  format(n_notifications, big.mark = ","),
  " -- carries no information until the day it does.\n\n",
  "Two date formats occur in one notification: the dates the register ",
  "indexes are `2026-09-10T00:00:00Z` while the prospectus issue date is ",
  "`2026-09-10 00:00:00.0`, so a reader parses per field rather than per ",
  "document.\n"))
```

## The spreadsheets beside the register

```{r sheets, results='asis'}
sheet_dir <- file.path(path_bronze, "sheets", report_snapshot)
sheet_files <- if (dir.exists(sheet_dir)) {
  list.files(sheet_dir, pattern = "\\.xlsx$", full.names = TRUE)
} else {
  character(0)
}

if (length(sheet_files) == 0) {
  cat(paste0(
    "The snapshot of ", report_snapshot, " holds none of the spreadsheets ",
    "ESMA publishes beside the register. They hold what the register does ",
    "not: the notifications of 2019 to January 2022 as they stood when the ",
    "list was frozen, the cancellations with ESMA's reasons for them, the ",
    "synthetic STS securitisations, which are notified by e-mail and are in ",
    "no register, and the two registered securitisation repositories with ",
    "their legal entity identifiers. Collect them with ",
    "`sts.collect_sheets('", config_path, "')`.\n"))
} else {
  cat(paste0("The snapshot holds ", length(sheet_files),
             " of the spreadsheets ESMA publishes beside the register.\n"))
}
```

```{r sheets-table}
if (length(sheet_files) > 0 && requireNamespace("readxl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # Each sheet carries a block of disclaimer rows above its header, so the
  # header is the widest row of the first twenty-five rather than the first.
  read_sheet <- function(path) {
    raw <- readxl::read_excel(path, col_names = FALSE, n_max = 2000,
                              .name_repair = "minimal")
    filled <- apply(raw, 1, function(r) sum(!is.na(r) & trimws(r) != ""))
    head_at <- which(filled == max(filled[seq_len(min(25, length(filled)))]))[1]
    header <- as.character(unlist(raw[head_at, ], use.names = FALSE))
    body <- raw[seq.int(head_at + 1, nrow(raw)), , drop = FALSE]
    names(body) <- ifelse(is.na(header) | header == "",
                          paste0("col", seq_along(header)), header)
    body[apply(body, 1, function(r) sum(!is.na(r)) > 1), , drop = FALSE]
  }

  held <- bind_rows(lapply(sheet_files, function(path) {
    name <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(path))
    rows <- tryCatch(nrow(read_sheet(path)), error = function(e) NA_integer_)
    tibble(Spreadsheet = name, Rows = rows,
           `Size (KB)` = round(file.size(path) / 1024))
  }))

  # The frozen list of notifications is the one that can be set against the
  # register, both naming a securitisation by the same identifier. The
  # comparison is counted here and said in the chunk below, output of a
  # chunk that is not `asis` being quoted rather than rendered.
  traditional <- sheet_files[grepl("traditional", sheet_files)]
  if (length(traditional) == 1) {
    sheet <- tryCatch(read_sheet(traditional[1]), error = function(e) NULL)
    column <- if (!is.null(sheet)) {
      intersect(c("Unique Identifier", "Unique Securitisation Identifier"),
                names(sheet))
    } else {
      character(0)
    }
    if (length(column) > 0) {
      listed <- unique(trimws(as.character(sheet[[column[1]]])))
      frozen_listed <- listed[!is.na(listed) & listed != ""]
      frozen_still <- intersect(frozen_listed,
                                trimws(notifications$securitisation))
    }
  }

  knitr::kable(held, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
               caption = paste("The spreadsheets collected on",
                               report_snapshot))
}
```

```{r sheets-overlap, results='asis'}
if (exists("frozen_listed")) {
  cat(paste0(
    "The frozen list of 2019 to January 2022 names ",
    format(length(frozen_listed), big.mark = ","),
    " securitisations. **", format(length(frozen_still), big.mark = ","),
    " of them are still in the register and ",
    format(length(setdiff(frozen_listed, frozen_still)), big.mark = ","),
    " are not** -- which is the measure of how much a register of current ",
    "state does not say, and the reason the snapshots of this Bronze layer ",
    "are kept.\n"))
}
```

## Sources

```{r sources, results='asis'}
cat(paste(c(
  paste("**The register.** ESMA's public register of STS notifications,",
        "read through the machine-to-machine services of the registers",
        "portal, which are documented at",
        "registers.esma.europa.eu/publication/helpApp and need no key. The",
        "register is held as a Solr index and queried by URL."),
  paste("**The law.** Regulation (EU) 2017/2402, the Securitisation",
        "Regulation, whose Article 27 has the originator, the sponsor and",
        "the special purpose entity notify ESMA that a securitisation meets",
        "the criteria of Articles 19 to 22 or 23 to 26, and whose Article 28",
        "has an authorised third party verify compliance."),
  paste("**The spreadsheets.** ESMA33-128-760, the notifications of 2019 to",
        "14 January 2022; ESMA33-128-761, the cancellations to 23 May 2022,",
        "with the reasons; ESMA82-402-39, the synthetic STS securitisations;",
        "and the register of securitisation repositories. All four are files",
        "on esma.europa.eu."),
  paste("**The pipeline.** The `sts` module of fincommons, which collects",
        "the register and the spreadsheets into the Bronze layer, one dated",
        "snapshot per run. The module's README describes the layout and what",
        "to expect of the data; this report reads the snapshots directly,",
        "there being no Silver layer yet.")),
  collapse = "\n\n"))
```
